title: strandflow-attn-sliding-window-kernel-with-segmented-rope-and-adaptive-kv-prefetch
author: Priya Kapoor
commits: feat(attn): implement strandflow sliding-window kernel with hybrid flash/stream backend
perf(scheduler): adaptive continuous-batcher that aligns slabs to sequence distribution
feat(kv): partial-prefetcher that materializes only hot KV segments
fix(ci): tolerate trace timing jitter in bench harness
docs: add strandflow performance page and rollout notes
description: Summary: Introduces the StrandFlow sliding-window attention kernel: a hybrid flash/stream implementation that fuses a segmented-rope/rotary transform with tiled attention paths and an adaptive continuous batching scheduler. Also adds a light-weight partial-KV prefetcher that materializes only hot segments to reduce memory pressure and preserve cold-cache latency. Motivation: Long-context workflows and mixed-request distributions cause either high latency (when prefetched aggressively) or high memory usage (when caching everything). Existing fused-attention kernels optimized for single shapes struggle with mixed length PLs and continuous-batching heuristics. This PR ships a kernel and scheduler changes designed to perform well across short and long sequences while integrating with Redwood's KV cache. What changed (high-level): Implemented a StrandFlow kernel (runtime/attn/strandflow_kernel.cu, runtime/attn/strandflow.h) that: 1) applies a segmented-rope rotary transform during tile load to remove a separate memory pass; 2) picks an execution path at runtime: width-tiled flash path for long windows and stream-fused path for shorter windows that benefits from register reuse; 3) exposes a small per-request hint to the continuous-batcher about preferred slab size. Adaptive continuous-batcher (runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp): 1) collects sequence-length histograms per route and dynamically aligns slab boundaries to the 75th percentile shape to reduce padding; 2) opportunistically coalesces pending requests when latency SLO headroom exists. Partial-KV prefetcher (runtime/kv/partial_prefetcher.cpp, runtime/kv/kv_store.h): 1) tracks recent KV segment accesses and prefetches only the hottest segments when a request indicates a long-context path; 2) emits metrics for prefetch/evict effectiveness. Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on p4d.24xlarge: - Short prompts (<=64 tokens): StrandFlow stream-path gives 1.35x throughput vs baseline flash-only kernel (p95 latency unchanged). - Mid-long prompts (512-2048 tokens): 18-25% lower p50 latency and 12-18% lower p99 with slab-aligned batching enabled. - Memory footprint: partial-prefetch reduces peak KV memory by ~22% on long-context mixes. End-to-end perf tests (bench/bench_attn_windowing.py) show 10-12% overall cost-per-token reduction for a mixed PL production trace. Backwards compatibility and safety: Kernel falls back to the existing flash kernel when device capability or shape constraints do not match. New continuous-batcher heuristics are opt-in behind a runtime flag 'adaptive_sliding_window' for staged rollout. Tests: Unit tests added for forward correctness and rotary/rope equivalence (tests/attn/test_strandflow_forward.py). Bench harness updated; CI includes GPU microbench stage (ci/run_benchmarks.yml). Review conversation (summary): - Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Great direction. Two asks: (1) can we make the slab-tiling heuristics deterministic in the first-class rollout to make reproduction easier? (2) clarify eviction policy interaction with dedicated pools." Author reply (Priya): "(1) implemented deterministic seeding and added a trace-replay mode in the bench harness; see ci update. (2) added comments and a small policy shim so Dedicated pool eviction respects tenant reservation; referenced in runtime/kv/kv_store.h." - Maya Chen: "Please add an opt-out API surface for users who require strict per-request latency." Author reply: "Added 'prefer_no_coalesce' request hint and documented behavior in docs/perf/strandflow.md." - Liam O'Connor: "Bench numbers look promising; add A/B rollout plan for Dedicated customers." Author reply: "Added rollout notes and migration checklist in docs/releases/notes-2026-02-25.md." CI and iteration: First CI run flagged a race in continuous_batcher when a coalesce window closed while a slab was being materialized; fixed by introducing a per-slab lock and bumping the coalesce window logic. Subsequent GPU benchmark runs passed; final CI: all checks green. Rollout & monitoring: - Feature gated via runtime flag and feature-flag rollout; gradual canary to 5% of traffic. - New metrics: strandflow.path.selected, strandflow.prefetch.hit_ratio, scheduler.slab.pad_waste. Alerting recommendations included in docs/perf/strandflow.md. Related work & references: ties to ENG-1912 (continuous batching roadmap) and ENG-2028 (KV prefetch strategy). Not a breaking change. Merge: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Diego and Maya. Release notes: "Introduce StrandFlow sliding-window attention kernel with segmented-rope fusion, adaptive continuous-batching alignment, and partial KV prefetcher — reduces cost per token for mixed-length workloads and lowers memory footprint for long-context traces."
notes: Rollout checklist: 1) enable feature flag on staging and run benchmark trace-replay; 2) enable partial-prefetch metrics and validate hit_ratio > 0.6 before canary; 3) canary at 5% then 25% with dedicated pool guardrails; 4) monitor slab.pad_waste and p99 latency for target routes.
release_notes: Introduce StrandFlow sliding-window attention kernel with segmented-rope fusion, adaptive continuous-batching alignment, and partial KV prefetcher. Expected impact: 10-15% cost-per-token improvement on mixed workloads, 18-25% p50 latency improvement on long sequences, ~22% KV memory reduction for hot-long traces.
